Q: How to increase the maximum number of opened editors in IntelliJ? A:

Settings | Editor | General | Editor Tabs | Tab limit.

You may also want to increase the recent files limit in Settings | Editor | General | Recent files limit if you are using the Recent Files (Cmd+E) feature.

Works for all IntelliJ IDEA platform based IDEs.

Q: Why can't this macro handle trailing comma? A:

From experimenting with the compiler, the actual behavior seems to be this:

  • $(...,)* requires the comma after every item: matches a,b,c, but not a,b,c

  • $(...),* requires that there is no final comma: matches a,b,c but not a,b,c,

  • $(...),* $(,)? allows the final comma to be optional: matches both a,b,c, and a,b,c

I've stopped using the second option altogether because sometimes cargo fmt will force a trailing comma (yes even inside a macro call).

Q: Expo React Native: How to play notification sound for 30 seconds on Android? A:

Playing sound for 30 seconds against standard notification best practices. There concept called Headless Background Notification - notification delivered on device but not shown in notification center.

Use them to receive alert then play sound normally.

Q: Why does removing elements from a list in a for loop in Python skip values? A:

Why it happens?

Think of it like a queue of people. You're walking down the line removing certain people. The moment you remove person #2, everyone shuffles forward; so person #3 is now where #2 was. Your eyes move to position #3, which is actually the old #4. You just skipped #3 entirely.

Python's list iterator works the same way; it tracks an index, not the actual elements.

What happens with your list step by step

numbers = [1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9]

  • Index 0 → 1 (odd, keep)

  • Index 1 → 2 (even, removed). List becomes [1, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9]

  • Index 2 → 5 — 4 was skipped! It slid into index 1 but iterator moved to index 2

  • Index 3 → 6 (even, removed). List becomes [1, 4, 5, 8, 9]

  • Index 4 → 9 — 8 was skipped! Same reason

The fix : use a list comprehension instead

numbers = [1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9]
numbers = [num for num in numbers if num % 2 != 0]
print(numbers)  # [1, 5, 9]

Or if you want to keep the loop style, iterate over a copy using [:]:

numbers = [1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9]
for num in numbers[:]:
    if num % 2 == 0:
        numbers.remove(num)
print(numbers)  # [1, 5, 9]

Golden rule: Never modify a list while looping over it directly. Always loop over a copy, or build a new list.
